1. Pick a separate place for it, away from everyday spending, and give it a name.
2. Set an automatic transfer for payday: $192.31, or your own pace.
3. Write down your finish-line date. On this plan it's payday 26: Fri Oct 8, 2027.

The math: 25 paydays of $192.31, then $192.25 on payday 26 = exactly $5,000.00. Halfway is payday 13 (Fri Apr 9, 2027).
Not $192.31 for you? $100 a payday gets there in 50 paydays. $250 gets there in 20.
A sample plan, not real results. Same amount every payday, no windfalls. Miss one? We'll show the catch-up math.
Every second Friday at 12 pm ET: the progress bar, one real-number lesson (Canada and US) and one move for that payday.

Follow @fullyfundedhq so you don't miss payday 1. Run your own numbers in the free Paycheque Split Calculator, link in bio.

posts.caption:
Get up to $2,000 for your kid's school, free. Here's how to claim the Canada Learning Bond.
🇨🇦 Canada series: rules below are for Canada.

1. Get your child a SIN (Social Insurance Number).
2. Open an RESP, a school savings account, with a provider that offers the bond. No deposit needed.
3. Ask for the bond when you open it. Already have an RESP? Ask if the bond was requested.

How much: $500 for the first eligible year, then $100 for each later eligible year up to age 15. Maximum $2,000. ESDC also pays $25 to help cover the cost of opening the RESP.
Who: kids born in 2004 or later from lower-income families. One eligible year is enough for the first $500 (Jul 2025 to Jun 2026: 1 to 3 kids, adjusted family income $57,375 or less).
ESDC estimates about two-thirds of those born in 2004 or after are eligible for at least $500. It only lands once someone asks for it.
Turned 18? You can apply yourself until the day before you turn 21. It applies in Quebec too.
Can you add $500 a year? The education savings grant adds 20%, plus 20% more on the first $500 if family income is $58,523 or less (2026).

Send this to a parent, or to anyone 18 to 20.

Source: canada.ca · Rules as of Oct 2026

General education only, not financial advice.

#resp #canadalearningbond #personalfinancecanada #parenting #moneytips

Reach more of your goals: write one if-then plan tonight.

Pick a cue you can't miss: "When I sit down with coffee at 7:30..."
Name the first move: "...then I open the draft and type one line."
Plan for the obstacle: "If my phone buzzes, then I flip it face-down."

Why: across 94 independent tests, if-then plans had a medium-to-large effect on reaching goals (d = 0.65). It was the only one of 5 famous focus rules we checked that fully held up. Habits took 18 to 254 days in the classic study (not 21), and one missed day didn't derail them.

Never guess a parking sign again. Snap the whole pole and ask one question.

1. Take one clear photo of the whole pole, straight on.
2. Paste the prompt below with your exact day and time.

posts.caption:
Know what's normal in your first 72 hours home, and when to call.

Watch 3 things, every day:
1. Wet diapers. By day 6, expect 6 or more in 24 hours.
2. Bleeding after birth. Call your care team if you soak 1 pad in an hour, twice in a row, or pass clots larger than an egg.
3. Baby's skin and eyes. Worried about yellowing? Call your care team. Don't wait it out.

Also common: many babies lose a bit of weight in the first few days and gain it back by around 2 weeks. Lots of crying, tears out of nowhere a few days in, and bleeding for up to 6 weeks are common too.
Still feeling low after 2 weeks? Talk to your doctor. That goes for both parents. Partners can get postpartum depression too.

Save this for your first night home. Send it to whoever's driving you home.

Source: Public Health Agency of Canada, Your Guide to Postpartum Health and Caring for Your Baby (canada.ca) · As of Oct 2026

General information only, not medical advice. Talk to your doctor, midwife or public health nurse.

posts.caption:
Your freedom number is your yearly spending × 25. Work yours out tonight.

Spend 30,000 a year: 750,000. Spend 40,000: 1,000,000. Spend 60,000: 1,500,000. Any currency. Same math.
Why 25? It's the 4% rule turned around: 1 ÷ 4% = 25. It's a rule of thumb from US market history research in the 1990s (William Bengen, 1994; the Trinity study, 1998).
Expect a pension or state benefit? Take its yearly amount off first. Spend 40,000 with a 10,000 pension: 30,000 × 25 = 750,000.
The catch: it's a rule of thumb, not a promise. Many planners use a lower rate to be safer (at 3.5%, it's about × 29), and it's before tax and fees.

Save this for later.

Source: Bengen (1994) and the Trinity study (1998), example math · As of Oct 2026

General education only, not financial advice.

#personalfinance #retirementplanning #investing #moneytips #financialindependence

posts.caption:
Make tonight's sleep safer: alone, on their back, in a crib.

1. Alone: nothing in the crib but baby. No blankets, pillows, bumper pads or toys.
2. On their back: for every sleep, naps included.
3. In a crib, cradle or bassinet, in the room where you sleep, for the first 6 months.

Then check the crib: a firm, flat mattress, a tightly fitted sheet and no gaps at the sides. Car seats, swings, strollers, sofas and adult beds aren't made for baby's sleep. If baby dozes off there, move them to their crib. No blanket and no hat indoors: simple, fitted sleepwear is enough.

Save this for every caregiver who puts baby down. Send it to the grandparents before their first sleepover.

Sources: Public Health Agency of Canada, Safe Sleep for Your Baby (canada.ca) and the Canadian Paediatric Society (caringforkids.cps.ca) · As of Oct 2026

General information only, not medical advice. Talk to your doctor, midwife or public health nurse.

posts.caption:
Wealthy people often borrow against their investments instead of selling them. Hear it pitched? Ask 3 questions first.

How it works: a loan secured by your investments, so they stay invested. Names differ: securities-based line of credit, portfolio loan, Lombard loan in Europe, loan against shares in India.
Why it appeals: in many countries, a loan isn't taxed as income, while selling can trigger tax on the gain. It's the idea behind "buy, borrow, die": hold for life, borrow to spend, rarely sell.
The catch: you pay interest, often at a variable rate. If the investments fall, the lender can demand more money or sell them for you, often at the worst time (a margin call). You can lose more than you planned. Rules and tax vary by country.
The 3 questions: What's the rate, and can it change? At what drop do you sell my holdings? What happens if I can't pay?

This is education, not a recommendation. Save this for the day someone pitches it to you.

Source: FINRA (finra.org) · As of Oct 2026

General education only, not financial advice.

#investing #personalfinance #wealthbuilding #moneytips #stockmarket

The catch: if they fall, the lender can sell. An example portfolio loan statement, any currency: investments 100,000; borrowed against them 30,000; sold 0; still invested 100,000. Slide 2 of 3. If you ever hear this pitched: 'Ask these 3 questions.' 1. What's the rate? Can it change? Many are variable, so your cost can rise while you hold the loan. 2. At what drop do you sell? Ask for the exact line for your holdings, in writing. 3. What if I can't pay? Ask about deadlines, fees and what you could still owe. Slide 3 of 3. The catch: 'Markets fall. Loans don't.' You pay interest, often at a variable rate. A fall can bring a margin call: add money or repay. The lender can sell for you, often at the worst time. You can lose more than you planned. Rules and tax differ by country.

posts.caption:
Get one real stretch of sleep: split the night.

"Sleep when the baby sleeps" is real advice. It works better with a plan:
1. Split the night in 2 shifts. For example, one of you is on until 2 a.m., then you swap. Off means fully off. Breastfeeding? Your partner brings baby to you, then takes over the diaper and settling.
2. On your own tonight? Ask a family member or friend to take one shift.
3. Cut the day's extras: fewer visitors, and hand off meals and housework.

Canada's postpartum guide says it plainly: "Share the nights with your partner, family member or a friend."
For the 3 a.m. haze: sofas and armchairs aren't safe for baby's sleep. Feel yourself drifting off? Put baby on their back in the crib, then lie down.

Send this to your partner, then pick your shifts tonight.

Sources: Public Health Agency of Canada, Your Guide to Postpartum Health and Caring for Your Baby (canada.ca), American Academy of Pediatrics (healthychildren.org) · As of Oct 2026

General information only, not medical advice. Talk to your doctor, midwife or public health nurse.

posts.caption:
Have kids? Write a will that names a guardian. Here's how, in 3 steps.

Without a will, the law where you live decides who gets what, and a court may decide who raises your children.
1. Choose a guardian and a backup, and ask them first.
2. Make a will that names them, with a lawyer or notary, or your country's official will service.
3. Check the beneficiary names on your accounts and insurance, and tell someone where the papers are.
Review it every 5 years and after big changes, like a new baby, a marriage or a move.
Rules differ where you live; check your country's official site.

Send this to someone who just had a baby.

Source: gov.uk (Making a will) and government.nl · As of Oct 2026

General education only, not financial advice.

#estateplanning #newparents #parenting #personalfinance #moneytips

Restart tomorrow, and start with one locked hour.

Name the fresh start: "Monday is Day 1."
Restart smaller: one hour, not a whole new routine.
Lock it with an if-then: "When I sit down after dinner Monday, then I start the timer."

Why: in a large data set of 11,912 students, the chance of a gym visit was 33% higher at the start of a week. The data is observational: it shows more starts on fresh starts, not that they last. That's why you keep it small.

posts.caption:
Partners: own 5 jobs in week 1, without being asked.

Start with 3 tonight:
1. Bring baby to every feed, then water and a snack for the parent who's feeding.
2. Take the after-feed: change the diaper, then settle baby on their back in the crib.
3. Take a night shift: diapers, bottles if you use them, rocking. Take turns.

Then add 2 more: you decide when visitors come and how many, and you run meals, laundry and other kids.
And check in on yourself, too. Partners can get postpartum depression as well. If you feel unusually down, talk to your doctor.

Send this to your partner before the due date. Save it for night 1.

Sources: American Academy of Pediatrics (healthychildren.org), Public Health Agency of Canada postpartum guide (canada.ca) · As of Oct 2026

General information only, not medical advice. Talk to your doctor, midwife or public health nurse.

posts.caption:
Get through a public meltdown: stay calm, keep them safe, hold your no.

1. Calm yourself first. Slow breath, ignore the onlookers. Shouting back won't end it.
2. Keep them safe. Near danger? Hold them firmly. If not, stay close and wait it out.
3. Hold your no. Giving in, or a treat to stop it, teaches that tantrums work.

Instead of a bribe: try a distraction ("Look, a dog!"), 2 small choices ("Hold the bananas or the bread?") or a quieter spot. Afterwards, praise the calm, specifically.
It's the age, not you: tantrums happen most between ages 1 and 3, and by 4 they're far less common.

Save this for the next grocery run. Send it to your co-parent so you both hold the same no.

Sources: NHS (Temper tantrums), American Academy of Pediatrics (healthychildren.org) · As of Oct 2026

General information only, not medical advice. Talk to your doctor, midwife or public health nurse.

#toddlerlife #toddlertantrums #toddlerparenting #parentingtips #parentingcanada

Get one focused hour tomorrow: follow this plan, minute by minute.

0:00 Say your if-then, turn Wi-Fi and data off, open one task.
0:45 Stop mid-sentence, write the next 3 words, then tomorrow's to-do list.
0:50 Walk with one question: walk for ideas, sit for answers.

Why: each move comes from research, from 94 tests of if-then plans to a 467-person trial that blocked phone data (for 2 weeks; we use 1 hour). The lab timings were different from ours, so treat the minutes as our version.
